title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00543
what_is_it: FAA Washington Operations Center incident notification regarding UAP sighting reported by multiple commercial aircraft near Denver, CO.
core_summary: On August 25, 2023, United Airlines flight 369 (Boeing 737 MAX 8, Newark to Las Vegas) reported 2-4 unidentified aerial phenomena described as white lights with a green hue moving in a circular motion above the aircraft at flight level 340 near Denver. Three other aircraft (CMP477, SWA5298, and N8TZ) reported similar sightings. Pilots reported the activity appeared near the Big Dipper constellation at high altitude, and no evasive action was taken.
interpretation_warnings: The reference to the Big Dipper constellation suggests the objects may have been at extreme altitude or could potentially be astronomical or satellite phenomena rather than nearby objects.
This is a preliminary operations center notification, not a completed investigation.
No radar data or sensor corroboration is mentioned — all observations are visual from pilot reports.
Four independent aircraft corroborate the sighting, which strengthens the observation but all were visual-only reports.
The circular motion described could be consistent with certain atmospheric or optical phenomena.

public_headline: Four Airline Crews Report Green-White Lights Above Denver at Night
public_tldr: This FAA operations center notification documents a UAP sighting on August 25, 2023, in which the crew of United Airlines flight 369 and three other aircraft reported seeing 2–4 white lights with a green hue moving in a circular pattern above them near Denver, Colorado. No evasive action was taken and no investigation findings are included — this is a preliminary incident report, not a conclusion.
public_narrative:
On the night of August 25, 2023, at approximately 12:25 AM Mountain time, the crew of United Airlines flight 369 — a Boeing 737 MAX 8 flying from Newark to Las Vegas — reported unusual lights to Denver Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC). The aircraft was cruising at flight level 340, roughly 34,000 feet, in the vicinity of Denver, Colorado (coordinates approximately 39.86°N, 104.67°W).

The crew described seeing 2 to 4 unidentified aerial phenomena: white lights with a green hue moving in a circular motion above the aircraft. Pilots noted the activity appeared near the Big Dipper constellation at what they judged to be high altitude — well above their own cruising level.

Three other aircraft — identified as CMP477, SWA5298, and N8TZ — independently reported similar sightings. No evasive action was taken by any crew, and no law enforcement was notified.

This document is an FAA Washington Operations Center incident notification — essentially an internal alert that something was reported. It is not a completed investigation. There is no mention of radar data, sensor corroboration, or any follow-up analysis. The document records what pilots saw and reported; it draws no conclusions about what the objects were.
public_caveats: This is a preliminary operations center notification, not a completed investigation or final report. No conclusions were reached about what the lights were.
All observations were visual-only pilot reports. No radar data or instrument readings are mentioned in the document.
Four independent aircraft crews reported the sighting, which adds weight to the observation — but all reports describe the same visual phenomenon without sensor backup.

The pilots' reference to the Big Dipper constellation suggests the lights may have been at extreme altitude or distance, which means satellite activity, atmospheric phenomena, or other high-altitude explanations cannot be ruled out.
There is minimal redaction in this document. The record is brief because it is a notification form, not because information was removed.
